items.title: Working with AI feels more like leadership than coding
items.why_it_matters: An experienced developer shares why coding with AI is shifting from writing syntax to managing an assistant—focusing on setting context, verifying output, and knowing when to course-correct. This is highly relevant to your goal of mastering 'direction' over typing. This week, try treating your next Claude Code session like a delegation meeting: write down the exact acceptance criteria before you prompt, and reject any code that doesn't meet them.

items.title: Find out what your coding agents cost you
items.why_it_matters: This open-source CLI tool helps you track exactly how much your AI coding agents are costing you in API tokens. Since you are using Claude Code heavily and want to optimize your development costs, monitoring this prevents unexpected bills. This week, you can clone the repository and run it alongside your next coding session to see your real-time token spend.

items.title: Make Claude Say Less
items.why_it_matters: A simple prompt configuration designed to stop Claude from writing long, conversational explanations and force it to output only the code or answers you need. This saves you time and reduces token usage during rapid development. This week, try adding these 'say less' instructions to your Claude system prompt or custom instructions to speed up your coding loop.

items.title: Ask HN: I created a web browser using Claude, everybody hates it
items.why_it_matters: An indie developer built an entire web browser using Claude, Gemini, and Codex, and shared the open-source repository despite facing harsh online criticism. It is a raw example of someone shipping a complex project using the exact 'vibe coding' method you use. This week, you can open their GitHub repository to study how they structured their codebase and handled state using AI-generated code.

items.title: LiquidGlassSkill: Claude skill to implement Apple Liquid Glass UI styles
items.why_it_matters: This is a reusable Claude 'skill' (a system prompt extension) designed to help the model generate clean, Apple-style 'liquid glass' UI components. It is directly compatible with your Next.js frontend work. This week, try pasting this skill file into your Claude chat and ask it to style a new component for your AI-ingest project.
